system_prompt:
You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your p4_pathway and
p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — BancorpSouth Bank / Cadence Bank realized record, ~3-5-year horizon (~2020-2022)

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. The surviving entity's own closing-era filings
> stated it would report to a different federal agency after closing (see below); this
> sub-dossier traces what is retrievable from SEC/EDGAR and reputable press. It
> contains no information about how the transaction was structured at closing.

## Public-reporting status after the transaction (feasibility-relevant)
- On November 20, 2017, BancorpSouth, Inc. (the pre-reorganization holding company)
  filed a Form 15-12B certifying termination of registration of its common stock under
  Section 12(g) of the Exchange Act and suspension of its duty to file reports under
  Sections 13(a)/15(d). [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-17-347262, Form 15-12B]
- A search of EDGAR's company filing index for CIK 0001299939 (the surviving bank
  entity, formerly named "BancorpSouth Bank"; see below) for Form 10-K returns zero
  filings. [SRC: https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001299939&type=10-K]
- This is consistent with the closing-era filings' own statement that, after the
  reorganization, the surviving bank would file its periodic and current reports
  (Forms 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K) with the FDIC rather than the SEC. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-17-271952, Form DEFM14A; SEC accession 0001193125-17-328144, Form 8-K]
- CIK 0001299939's own SEC/EDGAR filing history in and after the ~2020-2022 window
  consists of filings made in an investment-manager or beneficial-owner capacity
  (Forms 13F-HR, Schedule 13G/13G-A), not periodic reports filed by the entity as an
  SEC-reporting issuer. [SRC: https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001299939.json]
- The FDIC operates a public "Securities Exchange Act Filings" portal for
  FDIC-supervised institutions (efr.fdic.gov, redirecting to
  securitiesfilings.fdicconnect.fdic.gov); its existence was confirmed but no specific
  periodic filing from that system was retrieved for this dossier, so no audited
  financial scalar for the surviving entity is cited here. [UNVERIFIED]

## Corporate identity change within the outcome window
- SEC's EDGAR company database records CIK 0001299939's registrant name as
  "BancorpSouth Bank" from 2004-08-11 until 2021-11-10, and as "Cadence Bank"
  beginning 2021-11-10. [SRC: https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001299939.json]
- On October 29, 2021 (within the fixed ~2020-2022 outcome window), Cadence
  Bancorporation — a separate, NYSE-listed bank holding company headquartered in
  Houston, Texas, unrelated to the 2017 reorganization — completed a merger under
  which Cadence Bancorporation merged with and into BancorpSouth, with BancorpSouth
  surviving; in connection with the closing, BancorpSouth Bank changed its name to
  "Cadence Bank" and changed its NYSE ticker symbol from "BXS" to "CADE." [SRC: SEC accession 0001140361-21-035867, Form 8-K, filed by Cadence Bancorporation (CIK 0001614184)]
- Cadence Bancorporation's then Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Paul B. Murphy,
  Jr., ceased serving as an executive officer of that company and was appointed
  Executive Vice Chairman of the surviving entity; BancorpSouth's then Chairman and
  Chief Executive Officer, James D. Rollins III, was named Chairman and Chief
  Executive Officer of the combined company. [SRC: SEC accession 0001140361-21-035867, Form 8-K; SEC accession 0001140361-21-023608, Form DEFM14A]
- Under the merger agreement (as described in the Definitive Merger Proxy Statement
  Cadence Bancorporation filed July 7, 2021), for the 36 months following the
  merger's effective time the combined company's main office and bank headquarters
  would remain located in Tupelo, Mississippi, while its corporate headquarters would
  be located in Houston, Texas — the surviving entity's main/bank office and its
  corporate headquarters were split between the two pre-merger companies' home
  cities. [SRC: SEC accession 0001140361-21-023608, Form DEFM14A]
- The combined company's board was set at 20 members for the period until its first
  annual shareholder meeting — 11 who had been BancorpSouth directors and 9 who had
  been Cadence Bancorporation directors — after which it was to be reduced to 18. [SRC: SEC accession 0001140361-21-023608, Form DEFM14A]
- Cadence Bancorporation separately filed a Form 15-12B in November 2021 to terminate
  its own SEC registration in connection with the merger's completion. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-21-135505, Form 15-12B]

## Items sought but not found
- No SEC-filed audited annual report (Form 10-K) was located for the surviving bank
  entity (BancorpSouth Bank / Cadence Bank) covering any fiscal year within the
  ~2020-2022 outcome window; its FDIC-filed periodic reports, which the closing-era
  filings state exist, were not independently retrieved for this dossier. No net
  income, total-asset, or comparable financial-performance scalar for the surviving
  entity is cited here as a result. [UNVERIFIED]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- Because the transaction's own terms moved the surviving entity's periodic reporting
  from the SEC to the FDIC, no SEC-filed 10-K exists to document the surviving bank's
  financial trajectory over the ~2020-2022 window, and no such record was located
  elsewhere within the scope of this dossier. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-17-271952, Form DEFM14A; SEC accession 0001193125-17-328144, Form 8-K]
- The single best-documented event within the fixed outcome window is a further
  business combination: on October 29, 2021, the entity that had survived the 2017
  reorganization (by then still doing business as BancorpSouth Bank) absorbed Cadence
  Bancorporation in a merger, retained its status as the surviving legal entity, but
  adopted its merger partner's name ("Cadence Bank") and ticker symbol ("CADE"), split
  its main/bank office (Tupelo) from its corporate headquarters (Houston), and
  installed BancorpSouth's own then-CEO as the combined company's Chairman and CEO
  while the merger partner's CEO moved to a vice-chairman role. [SRC: SEC accession 0001140361-21-035867, Form 8-K; SEC accession 0001140361-21-023608, Form DEFM14A]

[SLICE END]
